answer: To deter Sybil attacks in an agent mesh monitoring sparrow flocks across a dune and rock ledge, nodes authenticate peers via radio-frequency transient fingerprinting. Receivers analyze microsecond transmitter turn-on distortions unique to each node's physical oscillator. An attacker cannot digitally clone identities, incurring verifiable hardware procurement costs for discrete transceivers. However, ambient thermal swings alter analog circuit responses, triggering false authentication rejections.
